outcomeNote: mishna statement with its own elaborating question; no dispute

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ יְצִיאוֹת הַשַּׁבָּת, שְׁתַּיִם שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע בִּפְנִים, וּשְׁתַּיִם שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע בַּחוּץ.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» The acts of «carrying out» from a public domain into a private domain or vice versa, which are prohibited «on Shabbat,» are primarily «two» basic actions «that comprise four» cases from the perspective of a person «inside» a private domain, «and two» basic actions «that comprise four» cases from the perspective of a person «outside,» in a public domain.
The mishna elaborates: «How» do these eight cases take place? In order to answer that question, the mishna cites cases involving a poor person and a homeowner.

segments.he: הֶעָנִי עוֹמֵד בַּחוּץ, וּבַעַל הַבַּיִת בִּפְנִים: פָּשַׁט הֶעָנִי אֶת יָדוֹ לִפְנִים וְנָתַן לְתוֹךְ יָדוֹ שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת, אוֹ שֶׁנָּטַל מִתּוֹכָהּ וְהוֹצִיא — הֶעָנִי חַיָּיב וּבַעַל הַבַּיִת פָּטוּר.
segments.en: «The poor» person «stands outside,» in the public domain, «and the homeowner stands inside,» in the private domain. «The poor person» lifted an object in the public domain, «extended his hand into» the private domain, «and placed» the object «into the hand of the homeowner.» In that case, the poor person performed the prohibited labor of carrying from the public domain into the private domain in its entirety. «Or,» the poor person reached his hand into the private domain, «took» an item from the hand of the homeowner, «and carried» it «out» into the public domain. In that case, the poor person performed the prohibited labor of carrying out from the private domain into the public domain in its entirety. In both of these cases, because «the poor person» performed the prohibited labor in its entirety, he «is liable and the homeowner is exempt.»

moves.summary: the mishna counts the carrying acts of Shabbat as two that are four inside and two that are four outside
the mishna asks how the eight cases arise
first two cases: the poor person outside places into or takes from the homeowner's hand and completes the transfer himself, so he is liable and the homeowner exempt

positions.claim: carrying acts on Shabbat are two that are four inside and two that are four outside; where the poor person alone performs the whole transfer he is liable and the homeowner exempt
